thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: dedicated-pool-eu-west-1: observed p99 for model=gpt-medium = 2.80s (SLO=1.0s). queue_depth spike to 380, streaming tail stalls observed. Autoscaler notifications: handshake_delay > 90s. Paging on-call.

alice.nguyen: ack — I'm oncall. Taking the page and joining. Adding myself to thread.

ben.smith: I'm here too, looking at metrics in Grafana. p95 is 0.65s but p99 spikes correlate with queue depth and many warmup cold-starts.

alice.nguyen: quick snapshot from metrics:
```
pool: dedicated-pool-eu-west-1
p95: 0.65s
p99: 2.80s
queue_depth: 380 -> baseline 20
inflight_streams: 260
warmup_rate: 0.3 nodes/min
autoscaler_lag: 74s (60s SLA)
```

carmen.ramirez: I see a big backlog on the matchmaking queue. Our warmup job is rate-limited by handshake timeouts, many nodes stuck in COLD->WARM handshake.

dave_support: Support reports multiple customers seeing streaming stalls and timeouts. Top ticket: AcmeInc (customer-id: C-784). They reported partial streaming (first chunk then stall).

elaine_pm: Any customer-visible SLO breaches being tracked? We need an initial impact score for status page.

alice.nguyen: Initial assessment: small-medium impact (some customers see degraded streaming p99), one enterprise reported partial timeouts (AcmeInc) — potential P1-customer exposure. Not a full outage but degraded UX.

ben.smith: Root signals: high queue depth + slow autoscaler warmup + handshake backoff. Looking at autoscaler logs now.

ben.smith: from autoscaler logs (tail):
```
[2023-07-03T12:12:14Z] scale_decision: need +8 nodes, current_nodes=12, target=20
[2023-07-03T12:13:52Z] handshake: node-57 failed (timeout)
[2023-07-03T12:14:00Z] warmup_rate_limited: concurrency limit reached
[2023-07-03T12:14:45Z] scale_apply_delay: 68s
```

alice.nguyen: manual mitigation: requesting manual scale to +10 nodes and increase warmup concurrency. Carmen, can runtime accept immediate pre-warm?

carmen.ramirez: Yes, we have a prewarm profile but it's gated by handshake concurrency; I can temporarily bump handshake parallelism to 50 and let prewarm run. That should reduce cold handshakes.

alice.nguyen: doing manual actions now:
- bumped pool target by +10 nodes via orchestration console
- temporarily set handshake_parallelism=50
- force-requeued warmup job

incident-bot: ACTION_LOG: alice.nguyen executed manual_scale +10 at 2023-07-03T12:17:05Z

ben.smith: Routing adjustments: enabling fallback routing to smaller model-compat (gpt-small-quant) for non-critical customers to reduce pressure on gpt-medium instances. This will lower cost but keep streaming available.

dave_support: Notifying affected customers: sending heads-up to AcmeInc support channel. ETA for mitigation?

alice.nguyen: early signs: queue_depth dropping from 380 -> 120 over the last 4 minutes after manual scale. p99 down to 1.45s. Still see tail stalls for some long streams.

ben.smith: Observed a subset of streaming sessions hitting "kv-cache coldpath" which increases per-token latency for long conversations. We'll instrument to catch session ids.

carmen.ramirez: extra telemetry added: enabling debug hooks for handshake path and kv-cache hits. Command I'm running:
```
curl -X POST https://internal.telemetry/api/track -d '{"tag":"handshake-debug","ttl":"10m"}'
```

elaine_pm: For status page: set incident to "degraded performance" and note we have manual mitigation in progress and partial customer impact.

alice.nguyen: agreed. I'll update status page after we confirm p99 stable below 1.0s for 10 minutes.

ben.smith: small follow-up: autoscaler metrics show a backlog of queued scale actions because the control plane's apply_rate is limited by a bug introduced in recent deploy (rate-limiter default changed). Creating quick revert.

carmen.ramirez: I can hotfix the rate-limiter config in control plane. Will deploy a small patch to restore previous apply_rate. This should prevent future manual overrides piling up.

alice.nguyen: ok, plan so far:
1) manual scale +10 (done)
2) increase handshake_parallelism (done)
3) route non-critical to gpt-small fallback (done)
4) hotfix control-plane rate limiter (in progress)
5) monitor p99 for 10m then de-escalate

dave_support: Outbound update to AcmeInc: "We've applied mitigations (scale up, routing fallback). Streaming should be recovering; we'll follow up with logs."

ben.smith: live checks:
```
# quick query
curl -s "https://metrics.internal/api/query?m=p99_latency&pool=dedicated-pool-eu-west-1" | jq '.value'
# returns: 0.98
```

alice.nguyen: p99 is 0.98s now. queue_depth 45. Continued monitoring.

incident-bot: NOTE: page acknowledged by alice.nguyen at 2023-07-03T12:19:03Z

elaine_pm: please capture RCA notes as we go. High level cause hypothesis: sudden external traffic burst + changed rate-limiter config in control plane causing autoscaler apply_delay, compounded by conservative handshake concurrency and kv-cache coldpath amplification.

ben.smith: agreed. I'll own the initial RCA doc and we will triage post-incident for followups:
- revert PR that changed control-plane rate limiter defaults
- improve autoscaler visibility on apply queue length
- increase default handshake_parallelism for burst profiles or add graceful prewarm pipeline
- add circuit breaker to route to fallback model earlier when queue_depth > threshold

carmen.ramirez: adding immediate action: implement a fast-path for handshake reattempts (reduce exponential backoff for warmup) as a short-term fix.

alice.nguyen: status: p99 stable sub-1s for 5m, queue_depth steady at ~40, streaming stalls reported by support decreased. I'm standing down but staying available for 30 minutes.

dave_support: Confirming AcmeInc reports stream resumed. I'll close ticket after 1 hour if no regressions.

sre-lead: Good triage and quick manual mitigation. Followups: schedule postmortem, include timeline, include customer impact matrix, assign owners: ben -> control-plane PR revert, carmen -> handshake prewarm improvement, alice -> autoscaler runbook update.

alice.nguyen: assigning action items in task tracker now. Will attach logs + timeline.

incident-bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED: automated alarms cleared at 2023-07-03T12:36:00Z. Root cause pending RCA.

sre-lead: closing notes: no SLA credit expected at this time but document impact. We'll aim to ship rate-limiter revert + autoscaler queue metrics within 72 hours.

ben.smith: adding one note — add an automated playbook trigger: if queue_depth > 200 AND autoscaler_apply_queue > 10 -> auto-scale with bypass_rate_limiter flag (requires safe guard).

alice.nguyen: thanks everyone. Follow-up meeting scheduled for 2023-07-04 09:00 UTC to review RCA and remediation plan.

(reacts: :thumbsup: from carmen.ramirez, :eyes: from ben.smith, :clap: from dave_support)
